title: Tech Salesstack Quadrant — On‑Prem Evaluation Playlet (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, engineer-friendly reference for SEs and platform sellers to run a 20–30 minute on‑prem evaluation with platform architects and infra teams. Focus: surface tradeoffs, capture capacity needs, and leave with a clear pilot scope (SLA, data flow, and rollback).

Audience:
- Platform architects / infra lead
- Head of SRE / security reviewer (if present)
- Seller / SE running the call

One-liner to open the meeting (speaker note):
"We help teams run consistent LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — this session is a 30‑minute technical checklist so you can decide if an on‑prem pilot makes sense and what the minimal non‑negotiables are."

Quadrant: Salesstack decision quadrant (handwave sketch to use as slide 2)
- X-axis: Data sensitivity (low -> high)
- Y-axis: Latency imperative (low -> high)
- Quadrant outcomes:
  - Top-right (High data sensitivity, High latency): Strong candidate for Private (on‑prem/VPC) + Dedicated fallback.
  - Top-left (High data sensitivity, Low latency): Private but ops-tolerant (batching, async).
  - Bottom-right (Low data sensitivity, High latency): Dedicated preferred.
  - Bottom-left (Low/medium both): Hosted API first, reserve private for compliance exceptions.

Quick lead questions (for the first 8–10 min):
- What are the absolute latency p95 targets for user-facing flows?
- Any must‑stay-in‑region / air‑gap / KMS requirements?
- Expected QPS and peak tokens/sec (example: 50 rps * avg 200 tokens)
- Bulk vs interactive mix (percentage of sync calls)
- Can you share a sanitized sample prompt shape or token distribution?

If they ask why Redwood vs building: two bullets
- Serving economics + fallbacks: we provide batching/cache/quantization suggestions + routing policies so you avoid micro-ops replatform cycles.
- Observability and rollout tooling: token-level cost + eval hooks so you can detect model regressions before users do.

Demo / PoC play (15 min canonical run)
- Pre-call prep (ask in advance): sample prompt shapes, expected QPS, security checklist owner.
- Live steps:
  1) Show quick network diagram (redwood private control plane -> customer control plane -> inference nodes).
  2) Walk through the onboarding checklist (credentials, KMS placeholder, minimal firewall rules).
  3) Show latency demo screenshot: 100ms median local test (example), then show degrade mode and fallback to smaller model.
  4) Show Console: per-route token cost, canary rollout toggle, tracing link.
- Demo script tip: keep one fallback story ready (e.g., switch to 8-bit quantized variant when overload hits).

Objection cheat sheet (short, bulleted comebacks)
- "We can host ourselves": Great — ask how you’ll maintain kernel selection/quantization profiles across model updates; we provide that as a managed layer to reduce ops debt.
- "Latency is our #1 concern": run the p95 canary locally with our profiling tool and we’ll tune batching/KV cache to hit target.
- "Security is non-negotiable": highlight KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and private control plane option — ask for security contact for a short checklist exchange.

Canary + Pilot acceptance checklist (use as handout)
- Functional: sample prompt outputs within quality threshold (agree upstream metric, e.g., exact match > 85% on canonical test set).
- Performance: p95 latency <= agreed SLA (e.g., 300ms) under agreed load.
- Operational: alerts wired to SRE, 30‑day retention on key traces, rollback guardrails in place.
- Security/compliance: encryption-at-rest + in-transit validated, KMS policy verified.

Metrics to capture during pilot (ask for permission to collect)
- Token throughput and cost by model variant (daily)
- p50/p95/p99 latency per route (sampled)
- Error rates and fallback triggers (per minute)
- Quality regression signals vs baseline prompts (automated eval run weekly)

Slide outline (6 slides for a short sell):
1) Title + 1-liner + expected outcomes from this 30-min session
2) Decision quadrant (visual) + call positioning
3) Minimal network/ops diagram for private deployment
4) Pilot acceptance checklist (playbook)
5) Live demo / screenshots + fallback story
6) Ask / next steps (scoping call, security review, timeline)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the conversation metric-first — platform folks respond to numbers.
- Bring up model variant pricing only after we have concrete QPS numbers.
- If buyer mentions offline batch jobs heavily, push Dedicated + caching conversation.
- Avoid deep model-architecture chat unless they ask — this is serving + ops talk.

Open questions / todo items for doc iteration:
- Create a stripped-down 1‑page security checklist (Lina?) -> link to Confluence page.
- Add sample JSON firewall rules snippet for on‑prem quickstart (Tomás to produce).
- Draft a 2‑line legal elevator for procurement (Arjun).

Linked artifacts to drop into the slide deck (placeholders):
- 1‑pager: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OnPrem-Quick-Checklist
- Demo repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/demo-onprem-quickstart
- Pilot ticket template: PROJ-456

Feedback request:
- SEs: run this once next week and add two tactical call notes back here (what tripped you up, which slide you needed).
- Product: confirm we can share the console screenshot (privacy concern).

Bottom line (ready-to-say):
"If data residency or latency are blockers, we can scope a focused on‑prem pilot in two weeks that validates performance and gives you a rollback path — if pilot shows cost/ops are heavier than expected, fall back to Dedicated and we provide the migration plan."
